summary: Tapered Shoulder Sleeves V2 replaces the uniformly scaled shoulder-to-elbow primitives retained by Visible Shoulders V1 with closed, project-owned procedural garment meshes. Each sleeve has a broad deltoid, a continuous taper toward the elbow, and a restrained cuff roll while continuing to follow the live solved shoulder-to-elbow segment.

root_cause.v1_shape_problem: The retained V1 sphere-derived sleeve kept a nearly uniform cross-section, so front and profile captures read as cyan shoulder balls rather than cloth-covered upper arms.
root_cause.retained_shape: An eighteen-ring, twenty-eight-sided axial garment surface uses a deterministic deltoid bulge and cuff roll over a narrowing base radius.
root_cause.authority: The existing solved shoulder and elbow points remain authoritative; the mesh changes silhouette only and does not invent or move joints.

renderer_evidence.technical_verdict: pass: guide and broadest-body front, profile, and rear captures show a broad deltoid tapering into a smaller cuff with no return of the missing-shoulder gap
renderer_evidence.photoreal_verdict: fail: the procedural garment still lacks production cloth folds, deformation, identity-specific tailoring, seam integration, and convincing wet-material response

validation.focused_python: 16/16 production-character and safety-gear source and review-lock contracts passed
validation.renderer_turntable: 5/5 identities captured with front, profile, and rear views

m5.result: 1/1 CrewAvatarPoseProduction passed renderer-enabled with 0 warnings and 0 errors

accepted: Both production shoulder sleeves now use a tapered garment silhouette instead of uniform spherical or capsule-derived volume.
All five roster identities meet the 550-vertex mesh guard and existing shoulder-anchor contract.
The PFD still has no flotation shoulder pads; the geometry remains part of the splash-jacket layer.
No animation, mass, collision, raft, water, rescue, or gameplay-force authority changed.
rejected_or_open: The V1 uniform sleeve silhouette is superseded by this evidence set.
The retained procedural garment remains visibly synthetic and is not final photoreal character art.
The cuff transition is abrupt in profile and needs production garment topology, skinning, and cloth deformation.
No named character-art reviewer or qualified whitewater guide has approved this evidence for release media.
open_gates: A named character-art reviewer must approve or replace the sleeve topology, torso integration, deformation, seams, tailoring, and wet-material response.
A qualified whitewater guide must approve shoulder range of motion and paddle-stroke biomechanics in motion.
M9 remains blocked by all wider human, platform, signing, media, clean-build, performance, and promotion gates.
